From Old Anatolian Turkish قالی (qalı), from Persian خالی, although the direction of the borrowing is uncertain. Ultimately likely from Old Armenian Կարին (Karin), a city which was famed for its rugs.
Has been compared to Karakhanid قَلِنكْ (kalınğ, “dowry”), Karakhanid خُلِنكْ (xulınğ, “motley silk fabric imported from China”) and various words having the sense 'thick' (reflected in Azerbaijani qalın).
Cognate with Turkish halı, Turkmen haly, Kumyk хали (xali).
From Arabic عَاهِل (ʕāhil). Cognate with Turkish ahıl.
